verificationChecklist.task: Verify RDS certificate bundle with rejectUnauthorized flag
Simulate connection pool load with pgbench

riskAssessment.preventionAdvice: Do not deploy pg 8.11+ without matching AWS RDS SSL certificate bundle.

outcome.errorLogSnippet: Error: self signed certificate in certificate chain (AWS RDS Postgres:5432) at TLSSocket.onConnectSecure. Max pool size drained (25/25 clients hung).
outcome.engineerResolution: Provided AWS global-bundle.pem in ssl config and tuned pool clients to 12. Fix verified.

feedback.actualOutcomeNotes: We rushed the minor driver upgrade thinking pg 8.11 was backwards compatible. It completely broke RDS TLS handshakes.
feedback.lessonsLearned: Always verify RDS CA bundle compatibility on any pg driver change.

riskAssessment.headline: Resembles Deployment #1: 'pg' driver upgrade previously caused AWS RDS connection pool exhaustion
riskAssessment.summary: In Deployment #1, updating 'pg' without explicit TLS CA configuration caused ECONNRESET dropouts and exhausted database pool connections under production load. Deployment #27 updates 'pg' to 8.11.3 in checkout-api.
riskAssessment.plainEnglishHeadline: STOP: This code change will crash user checkout and payments
riskAssessment.plainEnglishSummary: An engineer is trying to update the database connection tool (pg driver). But 6 months ago, that exact same update crashed our checkout system for 45 minutes because Amazon AWS rejected the security connection. Hindsight remembered this 92% match and stopped it before code was deployed.
riskAssessment.customerImpact: Customers trying to buy items will see "Payment Failed" or "502 Server Error". Checkout will be 100% blocked.
riskAssessment.businessRisk: Estimated ~$48,000 lost checkout revenue and ~45 minutes of customer downtime.
riskAssessment.simpleFix: Include the AWS RDS security certificate in the Docker build and deploy to only 5% of users (Canary) first.

historicalComparison.whatFailedThen: Strict TLS handshake failure on RDS PostgreSQL connection pool; 25/25 clients drained in 4 minutes
historicalComparison.rootCauseThen: pg v8.8+ enforces strict TLS handshake rejectUnauthorized by default, rejecting RDS intermediate CA
historicalComparison.resolutionThen: Configured rejectUnauthorized: false with AWS global-bundle.pem cert bundle and reduced pool max to 12
historicalComparison.outcomeThen: Full production outage with 502 Bad Gateway across checkout flow (45 mins customer downtime)
keyDifferences: Current deployment also includes connection pool keepAlive tuning

blastRadius.potentialImpact: Primary pool starvation and HTTP 502 responses
blastRadius.userFacingImpact: Customers cannot click "Buy Now" or finish orders
Credit card charges get stuck in processing queues
Warehouse shipments delayed by up to 2 hours

verificationChecklist.task: Confirm ssl.rejectUnauthorized setting matches RDS intermediate chain policy
verificationChecklist.plainEnglishTask: Step 2: Test that the database accepts our security credentials without crashing

verificationChecklist.task: Validate connection pool max limit (<= 12 clients per container instance)
verificationChecklist.plainEnglishTask: Step 3: Keep simultaneous database connections limited to 12 to prevent server overload

verificationChecklist.task: Run pgbench load test against canary replica before traffic shift
verificationChecklist.plainEnglishTask: Step 4: Send simulated shopping traffic to 5% of users to prove it works before full rollout

riskAssessment.preventionAdvice: Hindsight memory indicates high probability of database connection failure if TLS parameters are not explicitly set. Test TLS handshake in canary before 100% traffic shift.

commitMessage: db(users): add organization_uuid NOT NULL column to enterprise profiles table

riskAssessment.headline: Resembles Deployment #22: Database migration pattern carries ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table lock risk
riskAssessment.summary: Hindsight records previous migration locking the 12M row table for 47 seconds, exhausting active connections.
riskAssessment.plainEnglishHeadline: Warning: This database update will freeze the entire website for ~1 minute
riskAssessment.plainEnglishSummary: The code is adding a new column to the customer database table without a default value. In Deployment #22, doing this locked 12 million rows and froze the entire website for 47 seconds, showing errors to all visitors.
riskAssessment.customerImpact: Website will freeze and show "Service Unavailable" for almost 1 full minute.
riskAssessment.businessRisk: All active customer transactions frozen during peak hours.
riskAssessment.simpleFix: Make the column optional (nullable) first, so the database can update in the background without freezing.

historicalComparison.whatChangedThen: Added NOT NULL column without DEFAULT value
historicalComparison.whatFailedThen: 47 second ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on production table
historicalComparison.rootCauseThen: Full table rewrite required by non-null constraint without default
historicalComparison.resolutionThen: Used expand-contract pattern with batch backfilling
keyDifferences: Current migration script targets schema changes in user-service

blastRadius.userFacingImpact: Any user trying to save data gets an error spinner
